parts.article:
An early cultural tourist
 
In the 15th century, the Italian merchant Cyriacus of Ancona journeyed in search of the Mediterranean’s classical past. In doing so, he laid the groundwork for today’s cultural holidays.
 
(A) Today we take it for granted that we travel around the world to admire the monuments of the past. We prepare for such trips by reading about what we are going to see, set out on the journey with a good idea of how we will get there and where we will stay, and have a sense of what we will encounter on location. Cyriacus of Ancona (1391-1452), the first cultural tourist since antiquity, lacked these advantages when, in the first half of the 15th century, he sailed around the Mediterranean in search of the remains of Greek and Roman civilisations.
 
(B) Cyriacus first became fascinated by ancient monuments while walking in his home city Ancona and looking at the marble arch, erected in AD 115, to the Roman Emperor Trajan. He suddenly saw the culture in a new light. He no longer saw it as just a familiar and generally overlooked landmark, but as a doorway to the wonders of ancient imperial Rome. Not many people of Cyriacus’s time were interested in historical travel; they generally ignored old buildings and structures, or worse, dismantled them for their building materials.
 
(C) Cyriacus decided to see the world for himself and to record details of whatever other antiquities remained to be discovered. His training as a merchant did not prepare him for this vocation; he did not know ancient languages, history or art. However, he set out to solve these failings, first by learning Latin at the age of 30 and then adding ancient Greek. Having done this, he then set off on voyages around the Mediterranean to find, investigate and understand ancient cultures from their buildings, sculptures and inscriptions. Thus he became the first archaeologist and cultural tourist, predating other antiquarians by some 200 years.
 
(D) Travel in the 15th century, however, was anything but simple or enjoyable. Overland journeys by foot or mule along bad roads, under constant threat from bandits, were bad; voyages by sea were even worse. When the weather cooperated, sailing went relatively smoothly: ships proceeded along coasts from one recognisable landmark to another. However, when there was no wind, the ship did not move. Strong winds were no friends either; they drenched the ship with lashing waves and blew it off course. Water swamped the deck, splashed into the cabins and soaked mattresses, clothes and food. Remarkably, Cyriacus never complained about the miseries of travel. Optimistic by nature, he endured such hardships unafraid and saw opportunities where other people saw setbacks.
 
(E) Among many of the important records made by Cyriacus was his crucial documenting, in 1431, of the remains of Cyzicus, an ancient Roman city that had relied on commerce for its financial success. He hired a local person to take him to the site and then had to work out for himself the significance of the ruins he was looking at because there was no guidebook on ancient architecture to help him.
 
(F) Indeed, he had no contemporary knowledge about the ruins. Cyzicus had been a splendid city in its prime. Unfortunately, the area was highly seismic and in AD 123 the city was so devastated by a major earthquake that, when the Roman Emperor Hadrian visited it the following year, he was so saddened that he decided to subsidise a campaign to reconstruct Cyzicus. He made a substantial donation for a new temple to the Roman god Jupiter. Cyriacus thought the ruined city was awe-inspiring. He found the remains of the temple and examined it in great detail, looking for clues in ancient texts to help him understand what he was seeing. He sketched the great doorway adorned with carved foliage and mythological characters. Cyriacus’s account of this temple is the only record of this building, as in the following centuries it was entirely stripped of all its stonework and all that remains is its base.
 
(G) Cyriacus also visited mainland Greece, in 1436, when no one went to Greece in order to see the country’s ancient ruins. One of his destinations was the sanctuary of Delphi. The ancient Greeks considered Delphi as being situated in the most beautiful spot in Greece. When Cyriacus arrived at the site of Delphi, however, he found war, earthquakes and avalanches had all but obliterated its ruins. Determined to find any ancient traces, Cyriacus spent six days walking all over the area, peering at odd stone blocks sticking out of the ground, running his hands over inscriptions to trace fragments of words, and trying to puzzle out the few surviving structural remains. Climbing uphill towards the rocks that tower over the site, he came upon a theatre built into the slope. Soon after his visit, the site was buried by a rockslide and was not seen again until archaeologists began to excavate the area systematically in the late 19th century.
 
(H) Cyriacus had hoped to visit Egypt and Ethiopia, but he never got there. However, in his life he did record for posterity countless ancient monuments around the Mediterranean, paving the way for future archaeologists and cultural tourists.

questions.question: Cyriacus was unable to research his journeys before he left.

analyses.content: 你可能觉得他是个文化游客就一定会做研究，但注意原文明确对比了现代人的便利和他那个时代的局限性，他当时并没有提前了解目的地的条件 。

We prepare for such trips by reading about what we are going to see, set out on the journey with a good idea of how we will get there and where we will stay, and have a sense of what we will encounter on location. Cyriacus of Ancona (1391-1452), the first cultural tourist since antiquity, lacked these advantages when, in the first half of the 15th century, he sailed around the Mediterranean in search of the remains of Greek and Roman civilisations. (第2段)
原文说现代人会在出发前通过阅读做准备，而Cyriacus“缺乏这些优势”，这直接说明他在出发前没法像我们一样对旅程做研究 。

questions.question: The Roman Emperor Trajan built the city of Ancona.

analyses.content: 原文只提到了安科纳有一座“献给罗马皇帝图拉真”的大理石拱门，完全没提这座城市是不是图拉真本人建造的 。
你可能会把“献给图拉真的拱门（erected... to Trajan）”脑补成“图拉真建造了这座城市”，记住做判断题绝不能基于常识自己加戏 。
Cyriacus first became fascinated by ancient monuments while walking in his home city Ancona and looking at the marble arch, erected in AD 115, to the Roman Emperor Trajan. (第3段)

questions.question: Respect for ancient architecture was widespread in the 15th century.

analyses.content: 原文明确提到当时的人大多无视古建筑，甚至直接把它们拆了当建筑材料，这与题干描述的“普遍尊重古建筑”态度完全相反 。
即使你没注意到“dismantled”（拆除）这个词，只要看到“ignored”（无视），就已经足以判断出当时人们对古建筑并不尊重了 。
Not many people of Cyriacus's time were interested in historical travel; they generally ignored old buildings and structures, or worse, dismantled them for their building materials. (第4段)

questions.question: Cyriacus’s experience as a merchant gave him skills he needed to investigate the ancient world.

analyses.content: 题目说商人经历“给了他所需技能”，原文直接用“did not”打脸，不要看到 merchant 就想当然地以为“商业头脑肯定有帮助” 。
原文直接否定了这一点，明确说他作为商人的训练“并没有（did not prepare him）”让他为考察古代世界做好准备 。
His training as a merchant did not prepare him for this vocation; he did not know ancient languages, history or art. (第4段)

questions.question: Before leaving on his journey, Cyriacus studied ancient languages.

analyses.content: 原文提到他先学了拉丁语和古希腊语，这之后（Having done this）才启程航行，动作发生的先后顺序与题干“离开前学习古代语言”完全一致 。
你可能在找“before”这个词作为对应，但原文用的是“Having done this, he then set off...”，这是非常经典的先后顺序替换表达 。

However, he set out to solve these failings, first by learning Latin at the age of 30 and then adding ancient Greek. Having done this, he then set off on voyages around the Mediterranean to find, investigate and understand ancient cultures from their buildings, sculptures and inscriptions. (第4段)

questions.question: Travelling by sea in the 15th century was easier than travelling on land.

analyses.content: 原文明确对比了两者，说陆路很糟（were bad），而海路“更糟（were even worse）”，这与题干所说的“海路更容易”正好截然相反 。
做这类题只需要盯紧比较级，即使你看不懂陆路有什么具体危险，只要看到“sea were even worse”，就能直接判断题干说反了 。
Overland journeys by foot or mule along bad roads, under constant threat from bandits, were bad; voyages by sea were even worse. (第5段)

questions.question: Cyriacus tried to make his fellow sea travellers more comfortable.

analyses.content: Remarkably, Cyriacus never complained about the miseries of travel. Optimistic by nature, he endured such hardships unafraid and saw opportunities where other people saw setbacks. (第5段)
你可能觉得他既然自己很乐观坚强，理所当然会去照顾同伴，但在阅读判断题里，没有明确写出来的动作一律算作 NOT GIVEN 。
原文只提到他本人从不抱怨旅行的痛苦、非常乐观，但完全没有任何信息表明他是否试图去安慰或让其他同行的旅客感到更舒服 。

groups.description:
Do the following statements agree with the information given in Reading Passage 1?
In boxes 1–7 on your answer sheet, write.

groups.contentHtml:
Ancient Roman and Greek sites visited by Cyriacus
The city of Cyzicus
• The wealth of the city had come from .
• to the ancient city ruins was not available when visited by Cyriacus.
• The city was destroyed by a powerful in AD 123.
• A year later Emperor Hadrian supported a to rebuild the city.
• Cyriacus found part of the temple, which was built in the time of Emperor Hadrian, and made drawings of the to the temple and its decorative carvings.
The sanctuary of Delphi
• By the 15th century Delphi had almost disappeared due to natural disasters and .

analyses.content: 题干在问这座古城的“财富（wealth）”来自哪里，原文对应的是它的“经济成功（financial success）”依赖于“commerce（商业/贸易）” 。
填空题要注意词性，这里需要填名词，找到���relied on”后面的宾语“commerce”即可，定位非常直接 。

Among many of the important records made by Cyriacus was his crucial documenting, in 1431, of the remains of Cyzicus, an ancient Roman city that had relied on commerce for its financial success. (第6段)
题干说当时缺乏（was not available）关于遗址的什么东西，原文直接说因为当时“没有（there was no）指南（guidebook）”来帮他了解古建筑 。
注意题目要求“ONE WORD ONLY”，千万不要把 guidebook 拆成 guide book 两个词来写，否则直接算错 。

He hired a local person to take him to the site and then had to work out for himself the significance of the ruins he was looking at because there was no guidebook on ancient architecture to help him. (第6段)

Unfortunately, the area was highly seismic and in AD 123 the city was so devastated by a major earthquake that, when the Roman Emperor Hadrian visited it the following year, he was so saddened that he decided to subsidise a campaign to reconstruct Cyzicus. (第7段)
题干中的“powerful”对应原文的“major”，“destroyed”对应原文的“devastated”，导致城市被毁的原因直接填“earthquake（地震）” 。
这道题定位非常清晰，通过时间词“AD 123”可以瞬间锁定句子，注意抄写时不要拼错即可 。
题干中的“supported”对应原文的“subsidise（资助）”，“rebuild”对应原文的“reconstruct（重建）”，因此支持的行动填“campaign（行动/运动）” 。
你可能不认识 subsidise 这个词，但通过主语 Hadrian 皇帝以及后面的 reconstruct 也能猜出这是个支持重建的举措，抓准名词 campaign 填入即可 。

Unfortunately, the area was highly seismic and in AD 123 the city was so devastated by a major earthquake that, when the Roman Emperor Hadrian visited it the following year, he was so saddened that he decided to subsidise a campaign to reconstruct Cyzicus. (第7段)
题干问他画下了什么以及它的装饰雕刻（made drawings of... and its decorative carvings），原文提到他画下了（sketched）大“门道（doorway）”及其雕刻装饰，所以填 doorway 。
原文虽然有详细的“carved foliage and mythological characters”，但题干已经把这些概括为“decorative carvings”了，你要填的是被装饰的主体，千万不要填错词 。
He sketched the great doorway adorned with carved foliage and mythological characters. (第7段)
题干中已经给出了“自然灾害”（直接概括了原文提到的 earthquakes and avalanches），剩下的另一个导致遗址消失的并列原因就是“war（战争）” 。
不要把 earthquakes 或 avalanches 填进去，因为它们已经被题干里的 natural disasters 提前涵盖了，剩下的非自然因素只有 war 。
When Cyriacus arrived at the site of Delphi, however, he found war, earthquakes and avalanches had all but obliterated its ruins. (第8段)
